Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

response.message:
We’ll design the full Azure maintenance workflow, with versioned predictions and approval-only work-order drafts. Let’s first replay synthetic histories locally to check time splits, missing-sensor results, version records and duplicate approvals; mocked predictions test workflow behavior, while predictive quality needs a trained model evaluated on untouched held-out data, and Azure implementation remains engineering work.

proposal.title: Sketch the complete Azure maintenance qualification workflow
proposal.body: Adds ingestion, versioned data, feature preparation, training, held-out evaluation, model registration, prediction, drift monitoring and operator-approved work-order drafts. Azure Machine Learning owns its jobs, registry and endpoint within one service boundary; Azure Functions owns the qualification application's prediction orchestration and approval workflow. Batch replay is proposed for synthetic qualification; production cadence remains open. All cloud integrations require engineering: the available native generator does not implement this Azure ML application. Region, account access, service availability, identity configuration and connectivity are unverified. No deployment or tests have run. First local test: replay timestamped synthetic fixtures, including late maintenance labels, missing sensors and duplicate approval requests; assert point-in-time feature construction, explicit degraded results, version fields and one persisted work order per idempotency key. Scripted model outputs validate contracts only. Actual model validation requires training and evaluation on untouched later-period data, reporting false alarms and missed faults with thresholds still to be agreed. Synthetic evaluation alone does not establish real-equipment performance.

data.label: Synthetic sensor histories
data.description: External qualification fixture input, outside Azure provisioning scope. Timestamped equipment readings with deliberate gaps and late arrivals; fixture creation and location remain to be supplied.

data.label: Synthetic maintenance records
data.description: External qualification fixture input, outside provisioning scope. Equipment identifiers, maintenance events and candidate fault labels with event and availability timestamps; label meaning requires agreement.

data.label: Batch ingestion
data.description: Azure Data Factory pipelines ingest both fixture sources into versioned raw storage, validate schemas and equipment IDs, quarantine malformed records and record replay checkpoints. Source connectors, managed identity and retry policies require implementation and verification.

data.label: Versioned qualification data
data.description: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 stores raw snapshots, curated features, split manifests, model artifacts and evaluation reports under distinct paths. Preserve immutable dataset references and feature-code versions. Private access, scoped identities, retention and recovery need engineering and review.

data.label: Features, training, evaluation and prediction
data.description: Azure Machine Learning workspace owns feature jobs, training compute, MLflow model versions, evaluation jobs, a managed prediction endpoint and drift jobs; these are owned subresources, not separate conceptual services. Point-in-time joins use only information available at prediction time; split chronologically before fitting transforms, freeze a later holdout and report false alarms and missed faults. Register dataset, feature and model versions; controlled promotion requires reviewed evaluation. Endpoint returns explicit degraded status for missing required sensors. Drift jobs compare recent features and, when labels arrive, prediction errors; drift never automatically promotes models. Supervised fault labels, prediction horizon and thresholds remain open. Native implementation and regional support are unverified.

data.label: Prediction and work-order application
data.description: Azure Functions hosts authenticated operator routes, synthetic replay orchestration and work-order draft generation. Calls the ML endpoint and persists risk, degraded status, event time, dataset, feature and model versions. Presents drafts for explicit operator approval; uses an atomic conditional write and stable idempotency key to prevent duplicate approved orders. Degraded results require review. Returns prediction and draft details directly. No equipment control or external maintenance-system dispatch is included. Authentication integration, authorization, runtime storage and application code require engineering.

data.label: Prediction and approval ledger
data.description: Azure Cosmos DB stores versioned prediction records, draft revisions, approval identity/time and idempotency keys. Partition related workflow records by equipment; conditional updates and transactional operations within the partition enforce approval transitions and duplicate protection. Retention, backup and recovery settings remain to be agreed.

data.label: Maintenance operator
data.description: External human reviewer using an authenticated qualification client; no client application or identity is claimed provisioned. Reviews prediction evidence and degraded status, then explicitly approves or rejects work-order drafts.

data.label: Operational and drift alerts
data.description: Azure Monitor collects pipeline failures, endpoint errors, degraded-result rates, approval failures and custom drift/evaluation metrics. Alert routing, diagnostic settings, telemetry permissions, retention and response owner require implementation. Drift thresholds remain unconfirmed; alerts prompt investigation rather than automatic retraining or equipment action.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents training from using information unavailable when a prediction would have been made.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Time-based split prevents future-label leakage” and requested feature preparation.
requirementDrafts.statement: Construct features using event and availability timestamps, split chronologically before fitting transformations, and evaluate a frozen model on untouched later-period data, reporting false alarms and missed faults; acceptable thresholds remain open.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Avoids presenting incomplete sensor evidence as an ordinary reliable prediction.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Missing sensors produce an explicit degraded result”.
requirementDrafts.statement: Return and persist explicit degraded status when required sensors are missing, including the missing inputs, and present that status to the reviewing operator.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Makes each prediction traceable to the exact transformation and model used.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Prediction records include feature and model versions”.
requirementDrafts.statement: Persist feature and model versions with each prediction and retain references to the input dataset snapshot and evaluation evidence.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents unapproved actions and duplicate orders when requests are retried.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Work orders require approval and are idempotent” and “No automatic equipment control.”
requirementDrafts.statement: Create work orders as drafts, require an authorized operator's explicit approval, record the approval, and atomically prevent duplicate orders for the same idempotency key; provide no automatic equipment-control path.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Detects changing input patterns and prediction performance without treating a drift signal as permission to change the model.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Include ... drift monitoring” and held-out evaluation of false alarms and missed faults.
requirementDrafts.statement: Monitor feature drift and, when fault labels become available, prediction errors; route findings for investigation with model and feature versions attached, using thresholds and an operational owner to be agreed.
